newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Record Australia 96/97 rice crop at 1.4 MT - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: Record Australia 96/97 rice crop at 1.4 MT - ABARE.

text.p: Australia's 1996/97 (July/June) rice crop is expected to be a record 1.407 million tonnes (paddy), up 48 percent on 1995/96, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
Australian rice production in 1997/98 is set lower at 1.405 million tonnes on 157,000 hectares planted.
The production estimate reflected the record area planted of 166,000 hectares, up from 149,000 hectares the year before, ABARE said in its Australian Crop Report published on Tuesday.

In New South Wales, long grain rice production was estimated at 232,000 tonnes and fragrant rice production at 31,000 tonnes, with the remainder of the crop largely medium grain japonica rice, said ABARE, the government's main commodities forecaster.
Warm and dry conditions in March were ideal for harvesting, which was completed four months earlier than in 1995/96, ABARE said.
However, hot weather caused moisture content of the rice to drop too quickly, resulting in lower than expected milling yields, it said.
"Of further concern were logistical problems ... arising from the record harvest, with large scale receivals of up to 35,000 tonnes of rice a day causing long delays," ABARE said.
